newsitem.title: USA: New Blockbuster CEO named in bid to turn chain around.
newsitem.headline: New Blockbuster CEO named in bid to turn chain around.

text.p: Viacom Inc. Tuesday turned to an executive who's turned around a discount retailer and the Taco Bell fast food chain to fix its troubled Blockbuster video stores -- John Antioco.
Antioco will succeed Bill Fields, who resigned under pressure in April, when Viacom warned it expected earnings before taxes and other items to be off as much as 20 percent at Blockbuster.
Antioco had served as president of PepsiCo Inc.'s Taco Bell since last October.

Blockbuster, with 5,300 video stores, including 3,700 in the United States, has suffered from a lack of focus as it branched out into candy, movie-related toys and other merchandise, industry analysts said.

"Antioco's going to go back to basics," said David Doft, an analyst at Furman Selz. "He's going to focus on video rentals. He's known for his operational experience. That's something that Blockbuster needs right now."

Viacom Chairman Sumner Redstone acknowledged last week that other problems have also hampered the video retailer, including high costs, but said executives were working to fix the problems. Viacom bought Blockbuster from founder Wayne Huizenga for $8 billion in 1994.

"In the retail business, you're trying to figure out what's going to drive customers into the stores, how to sell it to them, and make sure they come back frequently, and he's done that," Bear Stearns analyst Steve Kernkraut said of Antioco.

Analysts said Fields wanted to turn Blockbuster stores into neighbourhood entertainment centres, selling licensed merchandise and music, soft drinks and candy. He also wanted to carry larger inventories of new movie releases.
But that strategy was based partly on his experience as an executive at Wal-Mart, whose stores are many times larger than Blockbuster outlets, analysts said.

Antioco made his reputation at Circle K Corp., which he joined in 1991. As chief executive, he led the company out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy, building the chain to 2,500 stores. Circle K was sold to Tosco Corp. last year.
"He was an excellent guy in running Circle K," said Kernkraut. "I have a high regard for him. He's a seasoned executive."
"He turned around the company," said Doft. "He has a great reputation in the retail business, and has a strong operations background."
William Franke, who was on the Circle K board that hired Antioco and is currently chairman of the airline America West Holdings Corp., said Antioco got valuable operations experience at Circle K.
While his stint at Taco Bell was short, "he pretty quickly grasped the issues at hand," said Janice Meyer at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
She said the fast food chain's first quarter sales at comparable stores rose 4 percent after two years of declines.

"You can't credit that to one person," Meyer said. "It was a team effort. But John was a good leader, who very quickly grasped some of the issues facing Taco Bell," including a pricing strategy in the competitive fast food industry.
